rationale: ROUND 2, revising on the same correlation after REVISE. All three objections were acted on; the migration was already APPLIED when the verdict arrived (config is live on apply), so this round reports what was checked in the world, not only what was argued. (1) editquality (medium) — I wrote into a key range a LANDMINE specifically covers and never cited it. Correct, and it is the sharper of the two process objections. Read since: the entry footprinted on `content_components.input_schema source: site_specs.identity.*` / `site_specs aspect='identity'` / the sites-table contact columns, which warns of a THREE-STORE ambiguity and prescribes: "put the three stores side by side in one query and read the row, not the shape — sites.email / site_specs.identity->>'email' / site_specs.identity->'contact'->>'email', per site", with `domain NOT LIKE 'pool-%'`. I had in fact run that comparison per site before writing (two stores of the three) — but I ran it without having read the entry, which is luck, not method. Run in full now, filtered as instructed, and IT CLEARS THE FIX: leopardessconsulting.co.uk holds the SAME address in all three stores (no ambiguity to resolve wrongly); robot-hands.com holds it ONLY in sites.email (which is precisely what alias step 2 reaches); gamesdesign.co.uk holds it in none of the three, so it resolves nothing and — because migration 538 gates the item — now renders nothing rather than an empty mailto. The landmine's warned-about case, stores disagreeing, DOES NOT ARISE on any affected site. Worth recording for the entry's next reader: that landmine's central claim is that the flat-vs-nested mismatch is real but 'not why the sites are broken' — true for bugs_open/072's population, and NOT true here. This is a different failure: the component names a different ASPECT (`contact`), which no alias bridges at all, rather than a different SHAPE within `identity`. (2) bug_historian (medium) — no check for OTHER fields on the same component that the same gate would silently fail. This one was already answered before the verdict landed, and by this very file's own verify block: its NOTICE census flagged 6 further active components declaring `site_specs.contact.*`, and chasing that found `contact_phone` (`site_specs.contact.phone`) and `contact_location` (`site_specs.contact.address`) on THIS component — and, at the served page, `` on 6 deployed rows across 3 sites. Fixed an hour later by migration 538 (council 1c8aed61): all three cb-detail-items gated on their own fields AND both siblings repointed. So the objection is right, and the answer is that the audit happened and shipped. (3) bug_historian (medium) — reconcile with 072. It is `bugs_closed/072_..._contact_info_reads_flat_identity_keys_the_writer_nests.md`, CLOSED 2026-07-31, fixed/approved/live/proven end-to-end (the corpus the seat read still lists it open — a LANDMINE on that very entry predicted this: it says the file 'stays in bugs_open/ until the chassis rolls', and it has since moved). Reconciliation: 072 IS the reason `resolveSpecAlias` exists — its step 1 bridges a component asking `identity.` flat to a writer that nests it, and step 2 falls back to the sites row. My change does not duplicate or compete with that; it ALIGNS a component that asks for a different aspect entirely with the spelling 072 made work. Adjacent, not overlapping. (4) bug_historian (low) — the NOTICE census only re-detects drift back to the same spelling, not other aspects mismatched against the single-aspect allow-list. Accepted as a real limitation; the general form belongs to RFC_042 (the shared-seam question), and this file deliberately does not widen the resolver.

edits.rationale: Repoint one field at the reachable spelling. Pre-flight asserts the single active row, the field, and the CURRENT source before any write, because a jsonb_set on a moved shape creates a branch and reports success. create_missing is FALSE deliberately: the key must already exist and the pre-flight proved it does, so a missing key is a moved schema rather than something to add. Verify asserts the source moved AND that type/required survived — jsonb_set replaces a subtree, and a path typo would silently drop the neighbours while the source read fine — plus a NOTICE census of any other active component still declaring a site_specs.contact.* source, since that aspect has never existed on any site.
edits.sketch: BEGIN; \echo BEFORE; DO $$ assert 1 active contact-block row (else RAISE naming RFC_034 fork rule) and contact_email.source = 'site_specs.contact.email' (else RAISE: already applied or schema moved) $$; UPDATE content_components SET input_schema = jsonb_set(input_schema,'{fields,contact_email,source}','"site_specs.identity.email"',false) WHERE id='4ebdccb5-...'; \echo AFTER; DO $$ verify source moved, type='text' and required IS TRUE intact, NOTICE on remaining site_specs.contact.* declarers $$; COMMIT; then a WATCH section: the per-site will-resolve-to query, the page_rerender (reason=section_data_resolved) needed to reach the artefact, and the divergence check first per bugs_open/229.

plan.risks: The address published is <site>@contactforsales.com on 15 of 44 sites and may be a platform-assigned lead-capture address rather than a client's inbox — publishing it because it is reachable is bugs_open/140's defect. Mitigated only by the owner's explicit 2026-08-21 ruling, which is quoted in the file header; without it the file must not be applied. Config is live on apply but no page changes until re-rendered, so 'applied' will not equal 'visible' — the header says so and the WATCH section carries the re-render step and the bugs_open/229 divergence check that must precede it. gamesdesign.co.uk will still not resolve (no email in either store). That is the correct outcome and is stated per-site in the header so a 5-of-6 result is not read as a partial failure. Reverting is NOT symmetrical and the ROLLBACK header says so: site_specs.contact.email resolves nowhere, so reverting restores a broken state deliberately; and it does not unpublish an address already re-rendered into content_data and deployed HTML — that needs the key cleared AND a re-render, and clearing only one of the two lets the PBP-039 carry re-supply it.
plan.non_scope: Not widening resolveSpecAlias to let any aspect read the sites row — shared-seam, RFC-shaped, and it would take the placeholder question fleet-wide. Not re-rendering the six pages in this change: config and artefact are sequenced separately on purpose, and each page needs its divergence stamp checked first (bugs_open/229). Not touching the other 3 of the 9 residual pairs: gamesdesign's cta.primary_url, leopardess's contact.cta_url, and fundamentallyai's six fields the component's schema no longer declares (bugs_open/309's class). Not minting review-queue items for any of them — six items that this one decision closes is the churn the two-strike rule punishes.
